newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Oct. 28, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Sun Microsystems Inc's Java programming language is a precocious development environment, not yet two years old, that is nudging the software development community away from its Windows focus, PC Week reported October 28.

Another quarterly loss at Borland International Inc - its fourth in the past eight quarters - plus two key management defections is making some analysts wonder whether the odds are too long to bet on Borland making a comeback, PC Week reported on October. 28.

COMPUTERWORLD - Companies seeking to upgrade older corporate software into applications ready to run on internal computer networks known as intranets are finding it easier in many ways to convert aging mainframe software applications than the newer generation of client/server software, Computerworld reported in its October 28 issue.
Microsoft Corp will lay out plans next week on building distributed applications that integrate its Windows NT desktop and server software with the Internet, Computerworld reported.

INFOWORLD - International Business Machines Corp plans to combine the interface of its OS/2 Warp 4.0 operatings system with Netscape Communications Corp's Navigator browser, InfoWorld reported in its October 28 issue.
Oracle Corp's long-delayed Oracle 8 database will go into beta testing late this year and is scheduled to ship in mid-1997, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - Tandem Computers Inc's launch of systems including cluster technology gives a boost to Microsoft Corp's promotion of its Windows NT for enterprise use, Information Week said in its October 28 issue.

MACWEEK - Apple Computer Inc programmers expressed disappointment with a memo from chief technologist Ellen Hancockthat failed to offer an alternative to the discarded Mac OS 8 strategy, MacWeek reported on October 28.
